brief.headline: Cut the PET bottle price by 16.6% to match our best supplier at ₹1.87/NOS and shift to 15-day payment to free up ₹46539 cash.

priceAsk.summary: Drop the amber PET bottle from ₹2.18 to ₹1.87 per piece
priceAsk.target: ₹1.87/NOS — closing the 16.6% gap saves us ₹28644 a year
priceAsk.basis: Suraj Blow Plast PVt. Ltd. sells us the same PET BOT AMBER 100ML/25MM NECK 12.5G at ₹1.87/NOS today. Market research shows PP caps at ₹0.85–0.95 typical, with room to ₹0.65–0.80 at scale — so TPAC's ₹2.18 sits high.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to 15 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹46539 for us — worth about 10.27% a year to them since they borrow at that rate, so offer it in exchange for part of the price cut.

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC is solid — they keep ₹3.80 of every ₹100 they sell, similar to peers at ₹3.70, carry very light debt at 0.19x, and hold an [ICRA] A / Stable rating. Their cash is stuck for 79 days, the same as similar firms at 79d, but they pay suppliers in just 17d while waiting 67d to collect — so cash moves slowly for them. We're tiny at 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue, which means on our own we have almost no pull — but their grey-zone distress score (2.77 Altman Z) and two compliance hiccups (GST filing delays, EPF payment delays) suggest some strain beneath the surface, so bundling volume or naming a strong second source will get their attention.

evidence.point: They sell us the amber PET bottle 16.6% higher than our best price
evidence.figure: Our price ₹2.18/NOS vs best ₹1.87/NOS (Suraj Blow Plast PVt. Ltd.), gap 16.6%, costing us ₹28644/year

evidence.point: They borrow money at about 10.27%, so paying them 15 days early is worth that rate to them
Their profit is in line with the industry but their cash gets paid out fast and comes in slow
evidence.figure: Net margin 3.8% vs peer 3.7%; they pay suppliers in 17d, collect in 67d, cash stuck 79d (peer 79d)

evidence.point: We're a very small customer with little individual leverage
evidence.figure: Our ₹11.32 L = 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue

evidence.point: Compliance delays and a grey-zone distress flag hint at operational stress despite the good rating
evidence.figure: Altman Z 2.77 (grey zone), GST filing delays, EPF payment delays; rating [ICRA] A / Stable

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100) — direct fit for pharma bottles and caps, already a second source for us on packaging

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist (Pearlpet brand) — a direct match for our PET bottle needs

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader covering pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong and profitable, a robust second source for bottles and closures

risks: At 0.02% of their sales we have almost no bargaining weight alone — bundle more SKUs, commit longer volume, or bring a credible alternate into the conversation to create real pressure.

Their Altman Z score of 2.77 sits in the grey zone and they've had GST and EPF payment delays — push too hard on both price and faster payment at once and you risk tipping a fragile supplier; phase the asks or tie faster payment to the price cut as a trade.
The PET bottle gap is clear at 16.6%, but our total annual excess is only ₹28644 — make sure the negotiation effort and any second-source qualification cost doesn't eat the saving.
Their 17d payable days mean they pay suppliers fast while waiting 67d to collect — so they may resist shorter terms from us unless we sweeten it with volume or a firm multi-year commitment.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to close the 16.6% gap on the amber PET bottle to the ₹1.87 we pay Suraj, and in return we can move to 15-day payment — which at your 10.27% borrowing rate puts real cash back in your hands faster.
